summary: Intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes when region-pinned traffic falls back to out-of-region egress
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent high latency (~200-800ms increase at p95/p99) for in-region requests when their routing falls back off the primary us-west pool into an out-of-region egress path. Impact: user-facing timeouts for inference calls in production, elevated token cost due to retrying. Timeline: 2026-03-09 17:40 UTC - customer began seeing spikes; 2026-03-09 18:05 UTC - first support contact; 2026-03-10 - triage opened and routed to SRE and Routing owners. This ticket covers investigation of whether egress policy, TLS session reuse, or cross-region routing orchestration is the root cause.
impact: Production inference calls for NimbusHealth show transient p95/p99 latency increases causing degraded UX during morning traffic peak. Estimated 8% of requests experienced >=200ms extra latency during incident windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure account with region-pin=us-west and low-tier fallback routing enabled
2) Send steady generation traffic (approx 30 requests/s) targeting rw-7b-instruct with short contexts
3) Simulate reduced capacity in us-west pool to trigger fallback routing
4) Observe end-to-end latency and trace headers (X-Trace-Id) for out-of-region routed requests
logs: Representative traces: trace-id=trc_20260309_7f3a; see traces page https://console.redwood/instrumentation/traces/trc_20260309_7f3a. API gateway logs show 0.6s increase before streaming token emission. SRE packet captures (pcap) uploaded to s3://redwood-support/sup-20347/pcaps.tar.gz. No obvious 5xx errors in serving-runtime, but TLS handshake times increase for some connections (full handshake observed vs resumed session).
comments: Priya (Support): Customer reports spikes align with their via-us-east backup route being used during small us-west pool drain windows.
Liam (SRE): Started correlation of routing decisions and TLS metrics. Noted a cluster of fallthrough requests where TLS session cache miss rate spikes from 2% -> 28%.
Customer (NimbusHealth): We only observe impact for model rw-7b-instruct and when our internal autoscaler reduces us-west capacity. We can disable fallback if that helps.

Elena (Routing Owner): Hypothesis: fallback routing creates a new egress path that terminates on a different edge NAT which doesn't have TLS session warm caches; also possible MTU/DF issues causing retries on segmented packets. Investigating netstack telemetry.
Liam (SRE): Added temporary routing rule to prefer nearest egress IP block for pinned fallthroughs. Monitoring for 2 hours to validate p95 improvement.
Priya (Support): Customer accepted temporary rule but requests a permanent solution and clearer docs about cross-region fallbacks and latency expectations.
investigation_notes:
Observations:
- Correlated spikes only on requests that were routed to out-of-region egress (us-east) after a brief us-west capacity shortfall.
- TLS metrics: session reuse dropped significantly for those requests; full TLS handshakes added ~120-350ms.
- Network path: out-of-region egress traverses a different edge NAT with distinct TLS session cache lifetime.
- No application-level 5xx; serving-runtime token generation time unchanged.
Hypotheses:
- Egress policy currently selects fallback region by availability, not by TLS session affinity; this can cause cold TLS handshakes adding latency.
- Edge-level session cache population is uneven across egress IP blocks.
- There may be an SRC IP NAT translation causing MTU differences that sometimes trigger additional packetization latency.
Next steps:
- Roll temporary preference to keep fallthrough egress in same region when available (done, monitoring).
- Add instrumentation to capture TLS handshake vs resumed percentages per egress IP block.
- Evaluate pre-warming/resuming TLS sessions for common customer pins during autoscaler events.
- Create runbook entry and customer-facing explanation about fallthrough latency tradeoffs.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary routing preference to select regional egress for pinned fallthroughs rolled out to NimbusHealth's account. Early metrics show p95 reduced by ~180ms for affected requests in the first hour. Final resolution pending: engineering change to ensure TLS session affinity and improved egress cache warm-up. Follow-ups: create a platform change to prefer TLS-session-affine egress when possible, update docs to call out expected latency delta for cross-region fallbacks, and add a config flag for customers to choose strict residency vs graceful fallback. NO final code PR merged yet; work tracked with linked PR and runbook updates.
notes_for_customer: Short term: we applied an account-level routing preference to keep fallthrough egress regional. Please monitor your 48-hour window and report any regressions. Long term: we will introduce TLS-session-affinity and a config toggle for strict residency fallback behavior. Documentation pointer will be provided once change is scheduled.
